question: Nursing informatics primarily combines nursing science with what other two fields?
explanation: Nursing informatics merges nursing knowledge with computer and information sciences to manage healthcare data effectively. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary clinical purpose of a patient health record in a hospital?

options.A: Serving as a legal and clinical repository of the patient's health journey
options.B: Providing marketing data for the hospital management board
options.C: Tracking the inventory of surgical instruments in the theatre
options.D: Calculating the monthly salaries for attending physicians and nurses

explanation: The health record documents all clinical care provided, acting as the primary legal and communication tool for the care team. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h1)

question: What is the main objective of implementing an Electronic Health Record system?

options.A: Eliminating the need for any nursing staff in outpatient clinics
options.B: Reducing the physical size of the hospital pharmacy department
options.C: Automating the collection of hospital utility bills
options.D: Providing instant access to patient data for authorized clinicians

explanation: EHRs are built to make comprehensive patient information immediately available at the point of care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h2)

question: An EHR differs from traditional paper records primarily because it enables what feature?

options.A: Permanently hiding past medical history from family members
options.B: Allowing patients to prescribe their own medications online
options.C: Removing the requirement for nurses to take vital signs
options.D: Sharing information across multiple healthcare providers and facilities

explanation: Interoperability allows electronic health records to be accessed and shared securely across different healthcare settings. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h2)

question: What was a major operational limitation of traditional paper-based patient charts?

options.A: They could only be accessed by one person at a time
options.B: They updated themselves automatically every twelve hours
options.C: They automatically translated notes into multiple languages
options.D: They required continuous electricity to remain legible

explanation: Physical paper charts can only exist in one physical location, restricting simultaneous review by multiple clinicians. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h3)

question: How do modern EHRs fundamentally differ from early digital attempts like scanned paper files?

options.A: Modern systems completely eliminate the need for clinical judgment
options.B: Early digital systems were completely immune to power outages
options.C: Scanned files required patients to write their own medical notes
options.D: Modern EHRs are dynamic databases supporting active clinical decisions

explanation: Dynamic EHR systems actively process data to assist with clinical workflows, unlike static scanned images of paper. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the function of an eMAR component within an EHR system?

options.A: Calculating the monthly utility expenses for the ward
options.B: Ordering new hospital furniture and medical equipment
options.C: Scheduling maintenance for laboratory diagnostic machines
options.D: Digital tracking of prescribed drugs, dosages, and administration times

explanation: The electronic Medication Administration Record tracks when and how drugs are given to patients. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h4)

question: A nurse receives an automated system warning about a potential adverse reaction between two prescribed drugs. Which EHR component generated this?
explanation: Clinical decision support systems analyze patient data to alert staff about allergies, interactions, and safety risks. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which system is best described as a digital version of a single clinic's paper chart?
explanation: An EMR is typically contained within one clinical practice and mirrors a traditional single-site medical chart. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the key advantage of an EHR over a standard EMR system?

options.A: An EMR automatically deletes data after patient discharge
options.B: An EHR can only be edited by senior medical consultants
options.C: An EHR is designed to share information across multiple healthcare organizations
options.D: An EMR requires expensive mainframe computers to operate

explanation: EHRs are built for interoperability, allowing data exchange across different facilities and provider networks. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h5)

question: What common hazard of paper charting is directly eliminated by using EHRs?

options.A: Physical fatigue among doctors during night shifts
options.B: The need for nurses to monitor patient vital signs
options.C: Dangerous guesswork caused by illegible handwriting
options.D: The requirement to obtain informed consent from patients

explanation: Digital text removes the ambiguity of poor handwriting, preventing medication and transcription errors. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h6)

question: How do EHRs assist public health monitoring during infectious disease outbreaks?

options.A: By automatically quarantining infected patients in their homes
options.B: By providing aggregate data to track disease patterns efficiently
options.C: By manufacturing vaccines directly inside the hospital pharmacy
options.D: By replacing community health extension workers entirely

explanation: Electronic systems allow quick aggregation of patient diagnosis data, helping authorities monitor public health threats. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is a major infrastructural challenge for EHR implementation in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Excessive speed of local internet service providers
options.B: Universal laws banning the use of digital devices in wards
options.C: Complete absence of computers in the entire country
options.D: Erratic power supply and frequent electrical grid failures

explanation: Unreliable electricity poses a significant barrier to maintaining continuous digital health record operations. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why does resistance from older personnel pose a hurdle during EHR adoption?

options.A: Senior nurses must pay for the software licenses out of pocket
options.B: Experienced staff are legally barred from touching computer keyboards
options.C: Digital systems are programmed to ignore input from veteran clinicians
options.D: Staff accustomed to paper routines may struggle or refuse to change workflows

explanation: Human resistance to workflow changes often slows down the successful adoption of new technologies. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which practice helps maintain data security when a nurse steps away from an EHR terminal?

options.A: Leaving the patient chart open for the next shift of nurses
options.B: Logging out or locking the computer screen immediately
options.C: Writing the password on a sticky note attached to the monitor
options.D: Turning off the main electrical breaker for the entire ward

explanation: Locking unattended terminals prevents unauthorized individuals from accessing sensitive patient health records. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h8)

question: What is the purpose of role-based access controls in an EHR system?

options.A: Ensuring every hospital worker can view executive financial records
options.B: Restricting user access only to information necessary for their specific job
options.C: Allowing patients to edit their own laboratory diagnostic results
options.D: Speeding up the internet connection speed for nursing supervisors

explanation: Role-based access ensures staff only see the data required to perform their specific clinical duties. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h8)

question: Which healthcare group typically spends the most time interacting with hospital EHR systems?
explanation: Nurses form the largest group of direct care providers and are the primary users of clinical documentation systems. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h9)

question: Why is the nurse's role in EHR management vital beyond simple data entry?

options.A: Nurses are solely responsible for writing the software source code
options.B: Nurses must repair broken computer monitors in the wards
options.C: Nurses handle the commercial marketing of the hospital database
options.D: Nurses critically evaluate data accuracy and advocate for patient privacy

explanation: Nurses ensure clinical accuracy and protect patient confidentiality while navigating daily digital documentation. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h9)
